definition: A linear operator is a mapping between two vector spaces that preserves the operations of vector addition and scalar multiplication.
details: A linear operator is a mapping between two vector spaces that preserves the operations of vector addition and scalar multiplication.

explainer.lead: A linear operator is a mapping between two vector spaces that preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication. It matters because this preservation property underlies the structure of many transformations used across mathematics and machine learning.

tiers.eli5: It is a rule that transforms arrows in a space without bending the rules of adding them or stretching them by a number.
tiers.practitioner: Represented and applied as structure-preserving mappings between vector spaces; a pitfall is assuming a mapping is linear when it does not preserve addition and scalar multiplication.
tiers.paperLevel: A mapping between two vector spaces that preserves the operations of vector addition and scalar multiplication.

explainer.example: A mapping between two vector spaces that sends sums to sums and scaled vectors to scaled outputs satisfies the definition.
